paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: The loss comparison between vanilla Transformer and the proposed SepLLM. SepLLM achieves lower loss different computation costs and different training time consistently.

annotations.annotation: The line plot illustrates the relationship between training time and the resulting loss during a training process. The x-axis is labeled "Training Time (s)" and is on a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 250,000 seconds with tick marks at intervals of 50,000 seconds. The y-axis is labeled "Loss" and also follows a linear scale, ranging from 2.40 to 2.75, with tick marks at intervals of 0.05. The plot features two lines: a purple line with a solid style, marked by triangles, representing the "Vanilla" method and a red line with a solid style, marked by circles, representing the "SepLLM" method. Initially, both lines start at a loss value of more than 2.75, with "Vanilla" slightly higher. As the training time progresses, both lines show a downward trend. By the end of the x-axis, the "Vanilla" line decreases to a loss of around 2.50, while the "SepLLM" line reaches approximately 2.49, suggesting a steady decline in loss for both methods. There's a green dashed line along the x-axis at loss of 2.5, which intercepts the red line and ends at end of purple line, and is marked in a green star. From these intercepts, two other green dashed line, perpendicular to the x-axis is given, these lines are of height Loss 2.56. And between these two lines, at the top, a green line parallel the x-axis is there, and a text "1.26x" is given on top. A legend is given top right.
